newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain may sell 33 pct of Endesa in 2 parts.
newsitem.headline: Spain may sell 33 pct of Endesa in 2 parts.

text.p: The Spanish government is studying the possibility of dividing into two segments the privatisation of a 33 percent privatisation of electricity firm Endesa this year, Industry Minister Josep Pique said on Tuesday.
Spain's holding company SEPI has a majority holding in Endesa of 66.8 percent, or 173.93 million shares, of which the government is expected to sell 33 percent this year.
"The public offering could be done in two different phases. Having seen the market demand, we could decide to increase the offer up to a ceiling of 33 percent," Pique said.
He said that with this method the government could prepare itself for any possible negative trend in the bourse, while keeping better control over market interest in the offer.
One possibility would be to start by offering an initial stake of around 20 percent.
If that proves successful, they can offer a second part later up to a maximum of 13 percent more.
SEPI said on Monday it had named Argentaria, Santander Investment -- a unit of Banco Santander -- and Merrill Lynch as global coordinators for the Endesa privatisation.
The statement added that the final details and design of the share sale would be set in October.
Argentaria has a 3 percent stake in Endesa while Santander has another 3.5 percent, but Pique ruled out that this may imply any conflict of interests.
